While inspecting systems and ductwork I discovered several points of concern.

- the 1st floor systems evaporator coil is dirty which in turn, is causing drain blowback as the blower is working harder. The water is not following its path down the coils into the drain pan and instead is falling onto secondary drain pan. This is where the rust begins. The moisture retained in the system also is causing the spread of bacterial growth in air handler. The muffler on condenser is rusting which could leak in the future. This is due to the age of the unit, and environment. It’s 13 years old. The system itself however, is functioning properly at this time.  I do recommend budgeting for replacement.

- The 2nd floor south side unit has a supply flex that is condensing because the connection is not sealed properly. The muffler on this condenser unit is rusted as well. It is the same age as the 1st floor unit. Recommend budgeting for replacement for this unit as well. System is functioning properly at this time.

- The 2nd floor Northside unit has a dehumidifier underneath in its return that wasn’t turned on. Engaged dehumidifier and set humidity to 45%. The filter needs to be replaced in dehumidifier. The ductwork on this unit is in very poor condition. It is condensing profusely on all flex runs and boots. Some flex runs have lost its integrity on the interior and appear collapsed from within. Boots are rusted out as well. This may be the result of a critter infiltrating attic at some point in time. There are signs of a rodent like critter chewing through insulation and allowing the warm air from outside to engulf attic space causing high humidity and condensation. Attic also has significant biological growth on lumber. Highly recommend replacing all ductwork as it has been compromised and adding a REME halo to nullify the effects of the biological growth. The system itself is functioning properly at this time.

- All accessible bathroom exhaust fans need backdraft dampers installed as well as being connected to the outside vent. This is where the rodent activity was at some point. The flexes are not connected to the outside vent and this is allowing warm air to infiltrate exhaust fan and cause the mildew on ceiling.
Please confirm if rodents/critters have been taken care of before any Tidewater Hospitality is done in the attic. Also areas that have been destroyed by animal must be re-sealed.
Section of ductwork may be difficult to access. Sheetrock may need to be removed to inspect bathroom exhaust fan and install backdraft damper that’s on the northside of house.

While conducting inspection I discovered several things.

- system 1 drain line is not properly sloped or trapped. The ductwork is old and condensing due to gaps and breaches in supply flexes to boots. There is also a supply grill on the return causing warm air from the attic to be conditioned as well as the air from the upstairs where the unit is designated to condition. Solutions - seal ductwork, run condensation pump, and remove grill from return.
-system 2 also has grill on return, and a supply flex is blocking the vent on the ptrap causing improper drainage. Solutions - remove return grill, and re route pvc vent.

- system 3 condensation line is configured improperly. There is a vent on this return as well. There is a supply vent on trunkline that should be removed as it’s dripping mastic and there is already a supply conditioning attic on system 2. Solutions - remove grill from return, remove grill from supply, and install a condensation pump.
System 4, 5, 6, and 7 are functioning properly at this time.
The dehumidifier is condensing profusely even though it is wrapped with insulation.
There are several spots in the attics spray foam insulation that should be blocked off, as it’s allowing warm air into where air handlers and dehumidifier is, causing condensation.
These areas should be covered, and a dehumidifier for the attic should be installed as there is hard caste and a soft caste mix of spray foam.
The dehumidifier for the attic will reduce the humidity levels in the area, eliminating condensing air handlers and dehumidifier.
The master bedroom should have had its own standalone unit, but instead it’s designated to system 3, which does two rooms and some of the living area downstairs.
All in all the installs of these systems are not great in my opinion, and a lot of these issues should not have existed.
